original_value: We present a novel negotiation model that allows an agent to learn how to negotiate during concurrent bilateral negotiations in unknown and dynamic e-markets. The agent uses an actor-critic architecture with model-free reinforcement learning to learn a strategy expressed as a deep neural network. We pre-train the strategy by supervision from synthetic market data, thereby decreasing the exploration time required for learning during negotiation. As a result, we can build automated agents for concurrent negotiations that can adapt to different e-market settings without the need to be pre-programmed. Our experimental evaluation shows that our deep reinforcement learning based agents outperform two existing well-known negotiation strategies in one-to-many concurrent bilateral negotiations for a range of e-market settings.

result.paraphrase: We introduce a novel negotiation model that enables an agent to learn how to negotiate in concurrent bilateral negotiations within unknown, dynamic e-markets. Using an actor-critic architecture and model-free reinforcement learning, the agent learns a strategy represented by a deep neural network. We pre-train this strategy with supervision from synthetic market data, reducing the exploration time needed for learning during negotiation. This lets us create automated agents for concurrent negotiations that adapt to different e-market settings without being pre-programmed. Our experiments show that these deep reinforcement learning agents outperform two established negotiation strategies in one-to-many concurrent bilateral negotiations across a range of e-market settings.
